name: OpenChamber
summary: Your OpenChamber sessions, approvals and usage in the notch
description:
OpenChamber puts the coding sessions you run in OpenChamber beside the notch. The shelf widget says what each one is doing in plain words, such as Running swift test or Editing Views.swift, with its model, agent profile and server, and how long the turn has run. Several sessions show at once: click one to open it in place, and hover what it is doing to read the whole command and its last message.

When a session asks for permission, a card appears on the notch with the exact command, and you allow it once or reject it without leaving what you are doing; the widget keeps every pending request, with Always for the ones you trust. Cards also tell you when a turn ends, fails or asks a question, unless OpenChamber is already in front.

The widget's Usage page shows a ring per provider with what is left of its tightest window, every window on hover, and a notice as one passes 80% and 95%.

It watches every server OpenChamber Desktop on this Mac is set up for, this Mac's own and your remote hosts, directly or through OpenChamber's relay, using the tokens Desktop already has, so there is nothing to pair.
